PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality defensive franchise with 70 consecutive years of dividend increases, strong brand portfolio, and consistent cash generation (operating cash flow $4.04B in Q3 FY2026). However, the near-term trajectory is mixed: Q3 FY2026 showed YoY revenue +7.4% and EPS +5.8%, but QoQ trends are negative (revenue -4.4%, EPS -8.4%) with sequential margin compression. The company faces real headwinds from ~$400M in after-tax tariff costs, rising commodity/oil prices (WTI back to $93), and a restructuring program targeting 7,000 job cuts. Valuation at 23x P/E sits in the lower half of its 12-month range (21.7-26.3), suggesting the market has partially priced in these pressures. The upcoming Q4 earnings on July 29 is a near-term catalyst, with consensus expecting EPS of ~$1.42 (a 10.7% decline), which could either confirm the trough or disappoint further. Balance sheet is solid (equity $54.7B, debt manageable for A-rated issuer). The score reflects a durable but slow-growth business facing temporary cost headwinds, trading at a modest discount to its own history, with a binary earnings event approaching that could re-rate modestly in either direction.
